relationships.subject: Zingiber officinale extract
relationships.evidence_quote: Water extracts of Z. officinale (100, 300, and 500 mg/kg, p.o.) significantly attenuated both cold and mechanical allodynia induced by oxaliplatin

relationships.subject: Zingiber officinale extract
relationships.evidence_quote: Water extracts of Z. officinale (100, 300, and 500 mg/kg, p.o.) significantly attenuated both cold and mechanical allodynia induced by oxaliplatin

relationships.subject: oxaliplatin
relationships.evidence_quote: In mice, a single oxaliplatin (6 mg/kg, i.p.) treatment induced significant cold and mechanical allodynia

relationships.subject: oxaliplatin
relationships.evidence_quote: the relative mRNA expression level (ratio of 5-HT1A receptor mRNA to GAPDH mRNA) of spinal 5-HT1A receptor was significantly decreased after oxaliplatin treatment

relationships.subject: Zingiber officinale extract
relationships.evidence_quote: Z. officinale administration significantly up-regulated the decreased mRNA expression level of 5-HT1A receptor

relationships.subject: NAN-190
relationships.evidence_quote: Pre-treatment with NAN-190 strongly blocked the anti-allodynic effect of Z. officinale on both cold and mechanical allodynia, whereas ketanserin failed to block this effect

relationships.subject: spinal 5-HT3 receptor
relationships.evidence_quote: 5-HT3 receptors were only involved in the cold allodynia-alleviating effect of Z. officinale

key_findings: Oral ginger water extract dose-dependently attenuates oxaliplatin-induced cold and mechanical allodynia in mice via spinal 5-HT1A (not 5-HT2A) receptors; 5-HT3 only for cold allodynia.
Oxaliplatin reduces spinal 5-HT1A receptor mRNA and ginger restores it.
